title: Chapter 159: Patient Number 8
html:
“This is revenge. He has a specific plan and target.” Possibilities raced through Chen Ge’s mind. The middle-aged man’s story revealed a great deal, and its details aligned with the clues he already possessed.

It perfectly matched one patient once confined in the Third Sick Hall: a doctor who became a patient after witnessing too many tragedies. Like the son in the story, he was dangerously violent. A name surfaced in Chen Ge’s mind—Xiong Qing.

Patient Number 8 had been diagnosed with hemispatial neglect and isolated as extremely dangerous. Because Xiong Qing was formerly a psychiatrist of above-average intelligence, his actions during an episode were far more calculated than most.

“Could he be the killer hiding in the hospital?” As both former doctor and patient, Xiong Qing knew the institution intimately and was entirely capable of arranging this.

“He knows the terrain, which gives him an enormous advantage.” Hemispatial neglect itself did not make Xiong Qing dangerous. His compulsion to impose his warped ideal of perfection on others did. In his mind, everything intact was wrong; even a physically perfect person required half their limbs broken before the body looked “correct.”

Most people with the condition recognized the flaw in their perception and tried to compensate for it. Xiong Qing instead sought to reshape everyone else according to his distorted vision.

For anyone trapped inside the hospital, losing even one limb could mean death. Chen Ge had found hair from four people but only three living captives. The missing fourth was probably dead already.

“It isn’t even midnight, and I haven’t reached the Third Sick Hall, yet trouble is everywhere. Tonight will be difficult.” This Three-Star Trial Mission far exceeded Murder by Midnight and Mu Yang High School. One mistake could cost him his life.

He had identified one likely killer but had never seen Xiong Qing. The twisted-faced figure could be Xiong Qing—or the middle-aged prisoner could be. The prisoner’s knowledge of the old man’s past made him particularly suspicious.

Crouching beside the old man’s cage, Chen Ge inspected its lock. All three were identical. Even if the middle-aged man had hidden a key, he could not launch a surprise attack under such close observation.

Rolling the mallet in one hand, Chen Ge met the prisoner’s eyes and asked directly, “How do you know so much about the old man’s life? Are you his son?”

“Me?” Hearing the suspicion, the man gave a bizarre reply. “I knew you would never believe me. None of you trust me, just as I trust none of you! Leave me alone. I hid all the way out here—how did you still find me? Stop watching my life!”

“None of us? Watching your life? What are you talking about?” Chen Ge struggled to follow.

“Every time I expose you, you wear that innocent expression. That is why you disgust me. I’ve seen through you, so why keep lying?” The man delivered the incomprehensible accusation with eerie composure. “What should I call you this time? Wang Xin? Xu Fei? Lee Yichang? Ma Yong? Or have you chosen another name?”

“What are you talking about?”

Chen Ge tried to calm him, but only worsened the outburst. “Now you’ll claim you don’t know any of those people—or me. Isn’t that right?”

“But I really don’t know any of you.”

“Stop lying! All of you are the same person wearing different disguises. Your false smiles disgust me. End this pointless game!”

“The same person in disguise?” The claim reminded Chen Ge of another patient in Doctor Gao’s files. Patient Number 5, Xu Tong, suffered from the Fregoli delusion. He believed everyone around him was a single persecutor in disguise and lived within a reality of his own invention.

The prisoner’s behavior matched Xu Tong’s diagnosis. He could converse normally until suspicion triggered his delusion, transforming coherence into paranoia within moments. Chen Ge had never dealt so closely with severe mental illness before.

Studying him behind the bars, another question arose.Why did the Third Sick Hall’s patients return here? Is something drawing them back, or are ghosts controlling them?

Asking Xu Tong directly would be simplest, but he was no longer capable of a rational conversation. Chen Ge turned to the young woman instead.

At his approach, she kicked the bars and tried to retreat. His flashlight revealed an ordinary-looking woman of about twenty, matching neither female patient described in the Third Sick Hall’s records.

“Both she and the old man were shaved. They must be the real victims.” He still did not understand the culprit’s fixation on hair. If this was revenge, perhaps someone had once subjected the culprit to the same humiliation.

“Relax.” He reached through the bars. The woman evaded him with desperate energy, but after three minutes of struggling, exhaustion forced her to stop.

“Believe me. I don’t intend to hurt you.” He gripped the pillowcase between her teeth and pulled it free.

The instant the gag came out, she shrieked into his face, “HAND! HAND! HAND!”

“What?”

Her voice was piercing. Whatever she had endured had shattered her. At the sound, the vacant old man abruptly collapsed and played dead.

Xu Tong’s frenzy vanished as well. He stared at the door with absolute concentration, terror filling his eyes.

“HAND! HAND…” The woman would not stop screaming, leaving Chen Ge no choice but to replace the gag.

“She’s mentally ill too.” The absence of a single stable person in the hospital deeply unsettled him.
